docs.title: MQTT Publish/Subscribe
docs.text: Send telemetry and handle a simple LED command via MQTT.

docs.title: Wiring
docs.text: • Broker: test.mosquitto.org (demo)

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
#include <WiFiS3.h>
#include <PubSubClient.h>

WiFiClient net;
PubSubClient mqtt(net);

const char* ssid = "YOUR_SSID";
const char* pass = "YOUR_PASS";

const char* host = "test.mosquitto.org";
const int   port = 1883;

const char* pubTopic = "stemsl/telemetry";
const char* subTopic = "stemsl/cmd";

void onMsg(char* topic, byte* payload, unsigned int len) {
  String s;
  for (unsigned int i = 0; i < len; i++) s += (char)payload[i];
  if (s == "led:on")  { pinMode(3, OUTPUT); digitalWrite(3, HIGH); }
  if (s == "led:off") { digitalWrite(3, LOW); }
}

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  WiFi.begin(ssid, pass);
  while (WiFi.status() != WL_CONNECTED) { delay(500); }
  mqtt.setServer(host, port);
  mqtt.setCallback(onMsg);
}

void loop() {
  if (!mqtt.connected()) {
    if (mqtt.connect("stemsl-ekr4")) mqtt.subscribe(subTopic);
  }
  mqtt.loop();

  static unsigned long t = 0;
  if (millis() - t > 2000) {
    t = millis();
    int v = analogRead(A0);
    String msg = String("{"a0":") + v + "}";
    mqtt.publish(pubTopic, msg.c_str());
  }
}

#include <WiFiS3.h>

const char* pass = "YOUR_PASS";

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  Serial.print("Connecting to ");
  Serial.println(ssid);

  if (WiFi.begin(ssid, pass) != WL_CONNECTED) {
    Serial.println("WiFi connect failed");
    return;
  }

  Serial.print("Connected! IP: ");
  Serial.println(WiFi.localIP());
}

void loop() {
  static unsigned long t = 0;
  if (millis() - t > 3000) {
    t = millis();
    int r = WiFi.ping("8.8.8.8");
    Serial.print("Ping: ");
    Serial.println(r);
  }
}

docs.text: Read ambient temperature and humidity.

docs.title: Wiring
docs.text: • DHT11 OUT→D8; VCC→5V; GND→GND

docs.title: Code

#include <DHT.h>

#define DHTPIN 8
#define DHTTYPE DHT11

DHT dht(DHTPIN, DHTTYPE);

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  dht.begin();
}

void loop() {
  float h = dht.readHumidity();
  float t = dht.readTemperature();
  if (isnan(h) || isnan(t)) {
    Serial.println("Sensor error");
    delay(2000);
    return;
  }
  Serial.print("T: "); Serial.print(t);
  Serial.print(" C  H: "); Serial.println(h);
  delay(2000);
}

docs.title: Ultrasonic Distance
docs.text: Measure distance using HC‑SR04.

docs.title: Wiring
docs.text: • TRIG→D4, ECHO→D7, VCC→5V, GND→GND

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
const int TRIG = 4;
const int ECHO = 7;

long microsecondsToCm(long us) { return us / 29 / 2; }

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(115200);
  pinMode(TRIG, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(ECHO, INPUT);
}

void loop() {
  digitalWrite(TRIG, LOW); delayMicroseconds(2);
  digitalWrite(TRIG, HIGH); delayMicroseconds(10);
  digitalWrite(TRIG, LOW);
  long duration = pulseIn(ECHO, HIGH, 30000);
  long cm = microsecondsToCm(duration);
  Serial.print(cm); Serial.println(" cm");
  delay(300);
}

docs.title: DIY Robot Dog Kit
docs.text: Robot Dog is an exciting and fun project for DIY robot builders. The robot only uses two servo motors yet it is able to accomplish full walking cycle and you can move it in four directions.

docs.title: 3. Back Leg Assembly
docs.text:
In this step, we will assemble the back legs of the Robot Dog and mount them on the second ice cream stick servo motor horn assembly prepared earlier.

The back leg assembly works together with the front leg assembly to create the walking motion of the Robot Dog.

docs.title: Parts Required
docs.text: Part Quantity Description Back legs 2 Cardboard back leg pieces Screws 4 Used to fix the legs to the ice cream stick / horn assembly Nuts 4 Used to lock the screws in place Servo motor horn assembly 1 Second servo motor horn assembly prepared using servo motor, horn, and ice cream stick

docs.title: 1. Identify the Back Legs
docs.text:
Take the two cardboard back leg pieces.

The back legs are similar to the front legs but will be mounted on the second servo motor assembly.

Keep both back legs in the same direction before mounting.

docs.title: 2. Place the Second Servo Horn Assembly
docs.text:
Take the second servo motor horn assembly.

Place it on the table with the ice cream stick facing horizontally.

This ice cream stick will act as the support bar for mounting both back legs.

docs.title: 3. Align the Back Legs
docs.text:
Place one back leg on the left side of the ice cream stick and the other back leg on the right side.

Make sure:

  • Both legs are facing the same direction.
  • The rounded ends are pointing downward.
  • Both legs are parallel to each other.
  • The marking lines on the two legs are aligned.
  • The legs are mounted at the same height.

docs.title: 4. Insert the Screws
docs.text:
Insert the screws through the holes in the back legs and ice cream stick.

Use two screws for each.

Do not fully tighten the screws immediately. First align both legs correctly.

docs.title: 5. Tighten the Nuts
docs.text:
Once both back legs are aligned, tighten the nuts gently.

The legs should be held firmly, but they should not be crushed or bent.

Avoid overtightening because it may damage the cardboard or restrict the movement.

docs.title: 6. Check the following
docs.text:
• Both back legs move together.
  • The legs do not touch the servo body.
  • The ice cream stick does not bend too much.
  • The screws and nuts do not block movement.
  • The servo horn remains firmly attached to the servo shaft.

docs.title: Back Leg Assembly Video
docs.text: Your browser does not support the video tag.

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
• Do not force the servo horn while checking movement.
  • Make sure the back legs are not mounted upside down.
  • Keep both legs at the same level.
  • Do not overtighten the nuts.
  • Keep the servo wire free so that it does not get pulled while walking.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Possible Reason Solution Back legs are loose Nuts are not tightened properly Tighten the nuts gently Legs are not aligned Legs moved while tightening Loosen, realign, and tighten again Servo horn is not moving freely Screws are too tight or touching the servo Adjust the screw position and loosen slightly One leg is higher than the other Uneven mounting Remove and mount both legs at the same height Ice cream stick bends Legs are misaligned or screws are too tight Realign the legs and tighten evenly Servo wire gets pulled Wire is trapped or twisted Free the servo wire before mounting to the body

docs.title: Completed Step
docs.text:
The back leg mechanism is now ready.

In the next step, we will check both the front leg assembly and back leg assembly together before fixing them to the Robot Dog body.

docs.title: 5. Assemble Body and legs
docs.text:
In this step, we will fix the front leg assembly and back leg assembly to the main body of the Robot Dog.

The body has two rectangular slots. These slots are used to position the servo motors. The rubber bands are used to hold the servo motors firmly in place on the body.

docs.title: Parts Required
docs.text: Part Quantity Description Body 1 Main cardboard body frame of the Robot Dog Front leg assembly 1 Front legs mounted on servo motor horn assembly Back leg assembly 1 Back legs mounted on servo motor horn assembly Rubber bands 2 Used to secure the servo motors to the body Screws 4 Used for fixing and alignment Nuts 4 Used to lock the screws in place

docs.title: 1. Identify the Body Orientation
docs.text:
Place the body part flat on the table.

The two rectangular cutouts on the body are used for positioning the servo motors.

Keep the body in the correct direction before fixing the legs:

  • Front leg assembly should be placed toward the front side of the Robot Dog.
  • Back leg assembly should be placed toward the rear side of the Robot Dog.
  • Servo wires should face upward or toward the inside of the body so they can be connected easily later.

docs.title: 2. Position the Front Leg Servo
docs.text:
Take the front leg assembly.

Place the front servo motor near the front rectangular slot on the body.

Align the servo motor so that:

  • The servo shaft faces outward.
  • The front legs hang downward freely.
  • The legs do not touch the body.
  • The servo wire remains accessible.

Do not tighten or secure it fully yet. First check the position and movement.

docs.title: 3. Secure the Front Servo Using Rubber Band
docs.text:
Use one rubber band to hold the front servo motor firmly on the body.

Pass the rubber band around the body and over the servo motor.

The rubber band should hold the servo motor tightly, but it should not press too hard on the servo wire.

Check that:

  • The servo motor does not slide.
  • The servo horn can still rotate.
  • The front legs can move freely.
  • The rubber band is not blocking the servo horn.

docs.title: 4. Position the Back Leg Servo
docs.text:
Take the back leg assembly.

Place the back servo motor near the rear rectangular slot on the body.

Align it in the same way as the front servo:

  • Servo shaft should face outward.
  • Back legs should hang downward.
  • Servo wire should be accessible.
  • The leg movement should not be blocked by the body.

docs.title: 5. Secure the Back Servo Using Rubber Band
docs.text:
Use the second rubber band to secure the back servo motor to the body.

Pass the rubber band around the body and over the servo motor.

Make sure the servo motor is held firmly in position.

Check that:

  • The servo motor is not loose.
  • The rubber band does not touch the moving horn.
  • The back legs can move freely.
  • Servo wire is not pulled or trapped.

docs.title: 6. Align Both Leg Assemblies
docs.text:
Place the Robot Dog body on a flat surface and check both leg assemblies.

Both front and back legs should:

  • Touch the surface properly.
  • Stand at a similar height.
  • Move without hitting the body.
  • Be balanced on both sides.

If the Robot Dog is tilted, loosen the rubber band slightly and adjust the servo position.

docs.title: 7. Tighten and Check Stability
docs.text:
After the position is correct, make sure the rubber bands are properly seated.

The rubber bands should keep both servo motors stable during movement.

Do not use glue at this stage. Keeping the servos secured with rubber bands makes it easy to adjust the position later if the walking motion is not correct.

docs.title: 8. Fold the Rectangular Cardboard Body
docs.text:
Fold the rectangular cardboard body along the marked fold lines to form the Robot Dog body shape.

The fold should create a firm rectangular body frame. Make sure the two rectangular servo slots remain open after folding.

docs.title: 9. Screw the Body in Place
docs.text:
After folding the rectangular cardboard body, use screws and nuts to lock the body shape.

Use:

  • 2 screws in the front side of the body
  • 2 screws in the back side of the body

Insert each screw through the matching holes in the folded cardboard and tighten it with a nut.

Do not overtighten the screws. The body should be firm, but the cardboard should not get crushed.

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
• Use rubber bands to secure the servo motors instead of permanently fixing them.
  • Do not overtighten the rubber bands, as this may bend the cardboard body or press the servo wires.
  • Make sure the servo horns are not blocked by the rubber bands.
  • Keep both servos aligned properly so the Robot Dog can walk smoothly.
  • If the Robot Dog does not walk correctly later, adjust the servo position and leg alignment.

docs.text:
The body and legs are now assembled.

In the next step, we will attach the head, neck, and tail to complete the Robot Dog structure.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
Make sure all parts are available before beginning the assembly.

You will need:

  • Micro:bit
  • Expansion board
  • Two servo motors
  • Front and back leg parts
  • Head, neck, body, and tail parts
  • Screws and nuts
  • IR sensor
  • IR remote control
  • Rubber bands
  • Ice cream sticks

docs.title: Assembly Overview
docs.text:
The Robot Dog is built in the following stages:

  1. Set the servo motor horns.
  2. Assemble the front leg mechanism.
  3. Assemble the back leg mechanism.
  4. Attach both front and back legs.
  5. Fix the legs to the body.
  6. Attach the head and neck.
  7. Mount the micro:bit and expansion board.
  8. Connect the IR sensor and servo motors.
  9. Upload the program and test the Robot Dog.

docs.title: Final Assembly of the Brain on to the Robot Dog
docs.text:
In this step, we will coneect the Brain with the servo motors and IR sensor.

The expansion board helps us connect the front leg servo, back leg servo, IR sensor, and power easily to the micro:bit.

docs.title: Brain Controller Installed on Robot Dog
docs.text: The image below shows the micro:bit brain controller installed on the Robot Dog and secured using the Velcro band.

docs.title: 1. Place the Brain Controller on the Body
docs.text:
Place the micro:bit and expansion board assembly inside the Robot Dog body.

Position the board so that:

  • The micro:bit buttons and display face forward.
  • The board sits safely inside the body.
  • The servo wires can easily reach the expansion board.
  • The IR sensor wire can reach the top/front of the Robot Dog head as shown in the above image.
  • The board does not touch the moving servo horns or legs.

docs.title: 2. Secure the Brain Using the Velcro Band
docs.text:
After placing the brain controller inside the Robot Dog body, use the Velcro band to hold it firmly in place.

Wrap the Velcro band around the Robot Dog body and the expansion board as shown in the image.

The Velcro band is important because it protects the brain controller from shaking or falling out while the Robot Dog is moving.

docs.title: Final Check
docs.text:
Before powering the Robot Dog, check the following:

  • Micro:bit is inserted in the correct direction.
  • All five screws on the micro:bit terminals are tightened properly.
  • Front leg servo is connected to P0.
  • Back leg servo is connected to P1.
  • IR sensor signal wire is connected to P2.
  • VCC and GND connections are correct.
  • Servo wires are not blocking the leg movement.
  • Expansion board power switch is in the OFF position before connecting power.

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
• Do not reverse VCC and GND connections.
  • Do not overtighten the screws on the micro:bit.
  • Make sure the servo connectors are inserted in the correct direction.
  • If the servo motor does not move, check the P0 and P1 connections.
  • If the IR remote does not work, check the IR sensor connection on P2.

docs.title: Completed Step
docs.text:
The micro:bit and expansion board are now assembled.

The Robot Dog electronics are ready for programming and testing.

docs.title: Time to play
docs.text: Now it’s time to have fun with your Robot Dog, test its movements, and experiment with it.

docs.title: Compare Front and Back Leg Assemblies
docs.text: In this step, compare the front leg assembly and back leg assembly before fixing them to the Robot Dog body. This check is important because both leg mechanisms must be aligned properly for smooth walking.

docs.title: Parts Required
docs.text: Part Quantity Description Front leg assembly 1 set Completed in the front leg assembly step Back leg assembly 1 set Completed in the back leg assembly step

docs.title: 1. Place Both Leg Assemblies Side by Side
docs.text: Place the front leg assembly and back leg assembly on a flat surface.

docs.title: 2. Check the Leg Direction
docs.text:
Make sure both leg assemblies are facing the correct direction.

The legs should be mounted in such a way that they can move freely when the servo rotates. If one leg assembly is reversed, the Robot Dog may not walk correctly.

docs.title: 3. Check the Screw and Nut Position
docs.text:
Inspect the screws and nuts on both assemblies.

Make sure:

  • Screws pass through the cardboard leg and ice cream stick properly.
  • Nuts are fixed securely.
  • No screw is loose.
  • Screws are not touching the servo body.
  • The cardboard legs are not bent or damaged.

docs.title: 4. Compare the Front and Back Legs
docs.text:
Both assemblies should look balanced.

Check the following:

Check Point What to Verify Leg alignment Both legs in each assembly should be parallel. Servo position Servo should be firmly attached to the horn and stick assembly. Height Both legs in the same assembly should be at the same level. Wire position Servo wires should not get pulled or trapped.

docs.title: 5. Test Movement Manually
docs.text: The legs should move smoothly without rubbing against the servo body or the ice cream stick.

docs.title: 6. Correct Any Misalignment
docs.text:
If the legs are not straight:

  1. Loosen the nuts slightly.
  2. Align the legs again.
  3. Tighten the nuts gently.
  4. Check movement again.

Do not overtighten the nuts, as this may damage the cardboard or restrict movement.

docs.title: Compare Both Legs Video
docs.text: Your browser does not support the video tag.

docs.title: Common Issues and Fixes
docs.text: Issue Possible Reason Solution One leg is loose Nut is not tightened properly Tighten the nut gently. Legs are not parallel Leg was fixed at an angle Loosen and realign the leg. Servo horn does not move freely Screw is touching the servo body Adjust the screw position. Assembly tilts to one side Legs are mounted unevenly Recheck alignment and height. Servo wire is twisted Wire was wrapped during assembly Free the wire before mounting.

docs.title: Completed Step
docs.text:
Both front and back leg assemblies are now ready.

In the next step, we will mount these leg assemblies on the main body of the Robot Dog.

docs.title: 2. Front Leg Assembly
docs.text:
In this step, we will assemble the front legs of the Robot Dog and mount them on the ice cream stick servo motor horn assembly prepared in the previous step.

The front leg assembly uses two cardboard front legs, screws, nuts, and the servo horn mechanism. This mechanism allows the servo motor to move the front legs forward and backward during walking.

docs.title: Parts Required
docs.text: Part Quantity Description Front legs 2 Cardboard front leg pieces Screws 4 Used to fix the legs to the ice cream stick / horn assembly Nuts 4 Used to lock the screws in place Servo motor horn assembly 1 Prepared in the previous step using servo motor, horn, and ice cream stick

docs.title: 1. Identify the Front Legs
docs.text:
Take the two cardboard front leg pieces.

Each leg has a rounded shape and a center marking line. The rounded end should face downward when the Robot Dog is standing.

Keep both front legs ready before fixing them to the servo horn assembly.

docs.title: 2. Place the Servo Horn Assembly
docs.text:
Take the servo motor horn assembly created in the previous step.

The ice cream stick should be fixed to the servo horn and should act as a support bar for the two front legs.

Place the servo motor on the table with the ice cream stick facing horizontally.

docs.title: 3. Align the Front Legs
docs.text:
Place one front leg on the left side of the ice cream stick and the other front leg on the right side.

Make sure:

  • Both legs are facing the same direction.
  • The rounded ends of both legs are pointing downward.
  • The legs are aligned evenly.
  • The center line on both legs is approximately at the same height.

docs.title: 4. Insert the Screws
docs.text:
Insert the screws through the holes in the front legs and ice cream stick.

Use two screws for each leg.

The screws should pass through:

Do not fully tighten the screws at first. Keep them slightly loose until both legs are aligned properly.

docs.title: 5. Tighten the Nuts
docs.text:
After both legs are aligned, tighten the nuts gently.

Make sure the legs are fixed firmly, but do not overtighten. Overtightening may damage the cardboard leg or restrict the movement.

docs.title: 6. Check the Leg Movement
docs.text:
Slowly rotate the servo horn by hand.

The front legs should move together smoothly.

Check the following:

  • The legs should not touch the servo body.
  • The legs should not be loose.
  • The ice cream stick should not bend too much.
  • The servo horn should remain fixed to the servo shaft.
  • The screws and nuts should not block movement.

docs.title: 7. Final Front Leg Assembly Check
docs.text:
Your front leg assembly is complete when:

  • Both front legs are mounted on the ice cream stick.
  • Both legs are parallel to each other.
  • Screws and nuts are properly tightened.
  • The servo motor can move the leg assembly freely.
  • The front legs are balanced and not tilted.
Your browser does not support the video tag.

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
• Do not force the servo horn while adjusting the legs.
  • If the legs are not aligned, loosen the nuts slightly and adjust again.
  • Make sure both legs are fixed at the same height.
  • Keep the servo wire free so it does not get pulled during movement.
  • The front leg assembly should be firm but should not be too tig

docs.title: 6. Assemble Head and Neck
docs.text: In this step, we will fix the head and neck parts of the Robot Dog. The head gives the Robot Dog its final shape, and the neck connects the head firmly to the body.

docs.title: Parts Required
docs.text: Part Quantity Description Head cardboard part 1 Front head section of the Robot Dog Neck cardboard part 1 Rectangular cardboard piece used to connect the head to the body Screws for head 3 Used to fix the head part securely Nuts for head 3 Used with the head screws Screws for neck 2 Used to fix the neck to the body Nuts for neck 2 Used with the neck screws

docs.title: 1. Identify the Head Part
docs.text:
Take the large cardboard head part.

The head part has two side flaps and a center face section. It also has marked fold lines and screw holes.

Keep the head part flat on the table and identify the fold lines before fixing it.

docs.title: 2. Fold the Head Shape
docs.text:
Fold the head gently along the marked fold lines.

Make sure:

  • The side flaps bend evenly.
  • The center face section remains in front.
  • The screw holes are aligned.
  • The folded shape looks balanced from both sides.

Do not force the cardboard while folding. Fold slowly along the marked lines to avoid damage.

docs.title: 3. Fix the Head Using 3 Screws and Nuts
docs.text:
Use 2 screws and 2 nuts to secure the bottom part of head shape.

Insert the screws through the matching holes in the head part and tighten them using nuts.

Use 1 screw for the top/center fixing point

Tighten the screw gently. The head should be firm, but the cardboard should not get crushed. Nut we will fix it after inserting this into the neck.

docs.title: 4. Identify the Neck Part
docs.text:
Take the rectangular cardboard neck piece.

The neck part is used to connect the head to the body. It should be folded along the marked line if required.

Make sure the neck piece is straight and the holes are aligned with the body.

docs.title: 5. Attach the Neck to the Body
docs.text:
Place the neck part on the front side of the Robot Dog body.

Align the holes on the neck with the holes on the body.

Use 2 screws and 2 nuts to fix the neck to the body at the bottom part of the neck

Tighten both screws gently so that the neck is firmly attached to the body.

docs.title: 6. Attach the Head to the Neck
docs.text:
Press the head the 1 screw centre point onto the neck support.

Align the head properly so that it faces forward.

Check that the head is centered and not tilted to the left or right.

If the head is fixed into the neck press gently until it fits properly. Fit the nut and tighten carefully.

docs.title: 7. Final Alignment Check
docs.text:
After fixing the head and neck, check the following:

  • The head is facing forward.
  • The neck is fixed firmly to the body.
  • The head is not loose.
  • The screws and nuts are tightened properly.
  • The head does not touch the moving legs.
  • The servo wires are not trapped under the head or neck.

docs.title: Head and Neck Assembly Video
docs.text: Your browser does not support the video tag.

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
• Use exactly 3 screws and nuts for fixing the head.
  • Use exactly 2 screws and nuts for fixing the neck to the body.
  • Do not overtighten the screws, as cardboard can get damaged.
  • Make sure the neck is fixed straight before attaching the head.
  • The head should not block the movement of the legs or servo wires.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Possible Reason Solution Head is loose Screws are not tightened properly Tighten the middle head screw gently Neck moves after fixing Neck screws are loose Tighten the 2 neck screws and nuts Head is tilted Head was not aligned before tightening Loosen, realign, and tighten again Cardboard bends or crushes Screws are overtightened Loosen slightly and adjust Head touches the legs Head or neck is mounted too low or tilted Reposition the neck and head

docs.title: Completed Step
docs.text:
The head and neck are now fixed to the Robot Dog body.

In the next step, mount the micro:bit expansion board, connect the servo motors, and prepare the Robot Dog for programming and testing.

docs.title: 1. Servo Motor Horn Setup
docs.text:
In this step, we will prepare the two servo motor horns used for the Robot Dog's front and back leg. Each servo motor must be fitted with a servo horn in the correct center position before assembling the front and back legs.

Use two identical sets of the parts shown below to create two servo horn assemblies.

docs.title: Parts Required
docs.text: Qty Part Use 2 Servo motors Used to move the front and back leg mechanisms. 2 Servo horn sets Used as the rotating arm attached to each servo motor shaft. 2 Small servo screws Used to lock the servo horn onto the servo motor shaft. 4 Medium servo screws Used to lock the servo onto the icecream stick. 2 Ice cream sticks Used later as support/link parts during leg assembly.

docs.title: 1. Identify the Servo Motor Parts
docs.text:
Take one servo motor set and identify the following:

  • Servo motor
  • Servo horn
  • Small screw for fixing the horn
  • Two screws for fixing the servo onto the icecream stick
  • Ice cream stick

Repeat the same for the second servo motor set.

docs.title: 2. Place the Servo Horn on the Shaft
docs.text:
Fit the servo horn on top of the servo motor shaft. Align it as shown in the assembly video.

Make sure:

  • The horn sits properly on the servo shaft.
  • The horn is not tilted.
  • The horn is aligned before tightening the screw.

docs.title: 3. Fix the Horn Using the Small Screw
docs.text:
Insert the small screw into the center of the horn and tighten it gently.

Do not over-tighten the screw. Tighten only enough so that the horn does not come loose during movement.

docs.title: 4. Repeat for the Second Servo Motor
docs.text:
Use the second servo motor set and repeat the same process.

At the end of this step, you should have:

  • One servo motor with horn fixed for the front leg mechanism.
  • One servo motor with horn fixed for the back leg mechanism.

docs.title: Final Check
docs.text:
Before moving to the next assembly step, check the following:

Check Expected Result Both servos have horns attached Yes Horn screws are fixed Yes Servo wires are not damaged Yes Horns are aligned as shown in the video Yes

docs.title: Common Mistakes to Avoid
docs.text: Mistake How to Avoid It Fixing the horn before centering the servo First calibrate the servo to initial position as explained in the brain controller section, then attach the horn. Over-tightening the screw Tighten gently until the horn is secure. Forcing the servo shaft by hand Use the program provided in brain controller section to initialize the servo position.

docs.text: Your browser does not support the video tag.

docs.title: Next Step
docs.text: After completing the servo horn setup, continue with the Front Leg Assembly.

docs.title: Assemble the Tail and Decorate the Robot Dog
docs.text:
In this step, we will attach the tail to the Robot Dog and then decorate the face creatively. This is the step that gives the Robot Dog its personality.

The tail is assembled to the slot at the back of the robot dog. After that, you can use sketch pens, markers, crayons, or colour pencils to draw the eyes, nose, mouth, ears, and other creative details.

docs.title: Parts Required
docs.text: Part Quantity Description Tail cardboard part 1 Cardboard tail piece of the Robot Dog Colour pens / markers As needed Used to decorate the Robot Dog face Pencil 1 Optional, for drawing the face outline before colouring Eraser 1 Optional, for correcting the pencil sketch

docs.title: Tail Part
docs.text: The image below shows the Robot Dog and the tail part.

docs.title: 1. Identify the Tail Slot
docs.text: Look at the back side of the Robot Dog. You will see a slot where the tail can be assembled.

docs.title: 2. Assemble the Tail
docs.text: Take the cardboard tail piece and assemble it into the tail slot

docs.title: 3. Adjust the Tail Position
docs.text: After inserting the tail, adjust it so that it stands upright.

docs.title: Tail Assembled on Robot Dog
docs.text: The image below shows the tail assembled on the Robot dog.

docs.title: 4. Decorate the Robot Dog Face
docs.text:
Now bring out your creativity and decorate the Robot Dog face.

You can draw:

  • Two eyes
  • Nose
  • Mouth
  • Tongue
  • Ears
  • Eyebrows
  • Cheeks
  • Spots or patterns
  • Name of your Robot Dog

Use a pencil first if you want to sketch lightly before colouring.

docs.title: 5. Creative Face Ideas
docs.text:
Here are some fun ideas:

Style What to Draw Happy Puppy Big eyes, smiling mouth, tongue sticking out Super Robot Dog Sharp eyes, lightning mark, bold outline Friendly Pet Round eyes, small nose, cute smile Space Dog Stars, antenna, space helmet style lines Police Dog Badge symbol, serious eyes, collar Cartoon Dog Large eyes, colourful ears, funny expression

docs.title: 6. Colouring Tips
docs.text:
Use light colours first and then add darker outlines.

Suggested colours:

Area Suggested Colour Eyes Black, brown, or blue Nose Black or dark brown Mouth Black or red Tongue Red or pink Ears Brown, orange, pink, or any colour you like Face outline Black marker Body patterns Spots, stripes, or your own design

docs.title: 7. Add Your Robot Dog Name
docs.text:
You can also give your Robot Dog a name.

Example names:

  • Robo
  • Bolt
  • Bingo
  • Spark
  • Bruno
  • Pixel
  • Chitti
  • Buddy

Write the name on the side of the body or near the head.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Issue Possible Reason Solution Tail is loose Tail is not inserted fully Push it gently into the slot Tail bends Too much force was applied Remove and reinsert carefully Tail touches servo wire Wire is routed too close to the tail Move the wire to the side Back legs hit the tail Tail is inserted too low or tilted Adjust the tail position Face drawing smudges Ink has not dried Allow the marker ink to dry fully

Your DIY Robot Dog is ready for final assembly

docs.title: Expansion Board and Micro:bit Assembly
docs.text:
In this step, we will assemble the micro:bit onto the expansion board and calibrate the servo motors

The expansion board helps us connect the servoe motors and power easily from the micro:bit.

docs.title: Parts Required
docs.text: Part Quantity Description Micro:bit 1 Main controller board Expansion board 1 Used to connect servo motors, IR sensor, and power Small screws 5 Used to tighten the micro:bit onto the expansion board Servo motor 2 Servo motor used for the leg mechanism

docs.title: 1. Place the Micro:bit on the Expansion Board
docs.text:
Take the micro:bit and place it on the expansion board as shown.

Make sure the gold edge connector pins of the micro:bit align properly with the expansion board terminals.

The micro:bit pins should match the labels on the expansion board:

Micro:bit Pin Expansion Board Terminal 0 P0 / 0 1 P1 / 1 2 P2 / 2 3V V / 3V GND G / GND

docs.title: 2. Tighten the Micro:bit Screws
docs.text:
After placing the micro:bit correctly on the expansion board, use the screws to secure it.

Tighten the screws on the following terminals:

  • P0 / 0
  • P1 / 1
  • P2 / 2
  • 3V / V
  • GND / G

Do not overtighten the screws. Tighten them just enough so that the micro:bit makes proper contact with the expansion board.

docs.title: 3. Connect the Servo Motor
docs.text:
Connect the servo motor to P0 on the expansion board and calibrate which is essential for leg assembly

Servo wire connection:

Servo Wire Connect To Brown / Black GND Red VCC Orange / Yellow P0 Signal

Make sure the servo connector is inserted in the correct direction.

Check the following:

  • Micro:bit is inserted in the correct direction.
  • All five screws on the micro:bit terminals are tightened properly.
  • First Servo Motor is connected to P0.
  • VCC and GND connections are correct.
  • Expansion board power switch is in the OFF position before connecting power.

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
• Do not reverse VCC and GND connections.
  • Do not overtighten the screws on the micro:bit.
  • Make sure the servo connectors are inserted in the correct direction.

docs.title: If You Want to Program It Yourself Using MakeCode
docs.text: Use this method if the robot program is not already pre programmed in the micro:bit.

docs.title: 1. Connect the Micro:bit
docs.text: Connect the micro:bit to your computer using a USB cable.

docs.text:
• Open the above program in https://makecode.microbit.org/ by clicking on Edit Code and clicking on the arrow.

  • Click download and program the code.

docs.title: Servo Motor Initial Position Setup
docs.text:
Before assembling the Robot Dog , both servo motors must be set to their initial position. This step is important because the servo horn position decides how the legs will move during walking.

Follow these steps:

  1. Insert the micro:bit into the expansion board.
  2. Connect the first servo motor to the expansion board.
  3. Turn ON the power switch on the expansion board.
  4. The servo motor will automatically move to the initial center position.
  5. Turn OFF the power switch on the expansion board.
  6. Do not rotate or disturb the servo shaft after it reaches initial position.
  7. Connect the second servo motor and repeat the same steps.
  8. Once both servo motors are set to initial position, continue with the assembly.

Warning

Do not disturb the servo horn or servo shaft after setting the servo to initial position. If the position changes, the Robot Dog leg movement may not work properly.

docs.title: Play and Experiment with Robot Dog
docs.text:
Now it is time to have fun with your Robot Dog, test its movements, and explore new experiments with your own robot pet dog.

You can control the Robot Dog in two ways:

  1. Using the Bluetooth Web Control App
  2. Using the IR Remote Control

docs.title: 1. Control Robot Dog Using Bluetooth Web Control App
docs.text:
The Robot Dog can be controlled wirelessly using the STEM Smart Labs Bluetooth Controller Hub.

Open the web control app:

https://remote.stemsmartlabs.com/

docs.title: Supported Platforms
docs.text:
The Bluetooth web control app works on the following platforms:

Platform Browser / App Requirement Windows Chrome browser with Bluetooth support Mac Chrome browser with Bluetooth support Chromebook Chrome browser with Bluetooth support iOS Bluefy Web BLE Browser iPadOS Bluefy Web BLE Browser

The browser or device should support Bluetooth 4.0 or higher.

docs.title: iPhone and iPad Support
docs.text:
For iPhone or iPad, use the Bluefy Web BLE Browser app.

Download Bluefy from the App Store:

Bluefy Web BLE Browser

iOS requirement:

  • iOS 13 or higher

docs.title: 2. Pair the Micro:bit
docs.text:
Follow these steps to connect your Robot Dog:

  1. Power ON the Robot Dog using the switch on the expansion board.
  2. Open the Bluetooth Web Control App:

https://remote.stemsmartlabs.com/

  1. Click PAIR MICROBIT.
  2. Select your micro:bit from the Bluetooth device list.
  3. Click Pair.
  4. Wait until the app connects to the micro:bit.
  5. Once connected, the app is ready to control the Robot Dog.

Tip

Keep the Robot Dog close to the computer, Chromebook, iPhone, or iPad while pairing.

docs.title: 3. Use D-Pad Controls
docs.text:
After the micro:bit is connected, use the D-Pad controls on the web app to move the Robot Dog.

D-Pad Button Robot Dog Action Up Move forward Down Move backward Left Turn left Right Turn right Center / Stop Stop movement

The Robot Dog will respond to the direction selected from the web control app.

docs.title: Keyboard Control
docs.text:
You can also use keyboard keys if supported by the web app.

Key Action W / Up Arrow Move forward S / Down Arrow Move backward A / Left Arrow Turn left D / Right Arrow Turn right Space Stop

docs.title: 4. Control Robot Dog Using IR Remote
docs.text:
You can also control the Robot Dog using the IR remote control.

Point the IR remote directly towards the IR sensor mounted near the top of the Robot Dog head.

Make sure:

  • The IR sensor is visible.
  • The IR sensor is not covered by wires or Velcro.
  • The remote is pointed towards the IR receiver.
  • The Robot Dog is powered ON.

docs.title: IR Remote Controls
docs.text:
IR Remote Button Robot Dog Action Forward Move forward Backward Move backward Left Turn left Right Turn right Stop / OK Stop movement

Note

If the Robot Dog does not respond to the IR remote, check whether the IR sensor is connected to P2 and aligned properly near the top of the Robot Dog head.

docs.title: 5. Experiment with Robot Dog
docs.text:
After testing the basic movements, try experimenting with your Robot Dog.

Here are some fun activities:

Experiment What to Try Walking test Check how smoothly the Robot Dog moves forward Turning test Test left and right turning movement Obstacle path Create a small path and guide the Robot Dog through it Remote challenge Control the Robot Dog only using the IR remote Bluetooth challenge Control the Robot Dog from the web app Speed tuning Modify the program to change the walking speed Step tuning Adjust servo angles in the code and observe the movement Creative design Add more colours, stickers, or a name tag to the Robot Dog

docs.title: 6. Safety and Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Use the Robot Dog on a flat surface.
  • Do not pull the servo wires while it is moving.
  • Keep fingers away from the moving legs.
  • Make sure the micro:bit and expansion board are secured using the Velcro band.
  • Keep the IR sensor facing forward or upward.
  • Turn OFF the power switch after use.
  • If the legs get stuck, turn OFF the power before adjusting them.

docs.title: 7. Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Possible Reason Solution Web app does not find micro:bit Bluetooth is off or micro:bit is not powered Turn ON Bluetooth and power ON the Robot Dog Micro:bit pairs but does not respond Program may not be loaded correctly Recheck and upload the Robot Dog program Robot Dog moves in wrong direction Servo connections may be swapped Check front servo on P0 and back servo on P1 IR remote does not work IR sensor is blocked or misaligned Point the IR sensor towards the remote Only one servo moves Servo wire is loose Check P0 and P1 servo connections Robot Dog stops suddenly Power may be low Replace or recharge the battery

docs.title: Completed
docs.text:
Congratulations! You have successfully built and tested your own Robot Dog.

Enjoy playing and experimenting with your own robot pet dog.

docs.title: DIY Robot Dog Top Kit
docs.text:
The DIY Robot Dog Top Kit is an exciting and engaging project for young innovators and DIY robotics enthusiasts. Powered by a single servo motor, the kit brings the robot to life by enabling synchronized head and tail movements.

The assembled top kit can be easily mounted onto the DIY Robot Dog Base Kit to create a complete, interactive robotic pet. This hands-on project offers a fun way to explore robotics, servo motor control, and mechanical movement

docs.title: Robot Dog Top Assembly
docs.text: Let's build the head and tail section of your Robot Dog! Before assembling anything, lay out the parts and match them with the numbers in the picture.

docs.title: Parts Included in the Kit
docs.text: The image below shows all the parts required to build the top part of the DIY Robot Dog.

docs.title: Parts Identification
docs.text:
No. Part Description and purpose 1 Trunk The trunk cardboard piece with fold lines, mounting holes, and a rectangular opening. It forms the main folded structure that supports the head-and-tail assembly. 2 Neck Neck cardboard piece with several holes and marked fold lines. 3 Tail Tail narrow strip with two visible mounting holes. 4 Servo Motor Connector Rounded-rectangle pieces for connecting the Servo Motor. These cardboard sections need to be joined to head and tail and will control the movement. 5 Screws, nuts, and plastic fasteners Metal screws and nuts, plus white plastic fasteners. Use the appropriate pieces to secure the cardboard parts and any moving connections. 6 Robot Dog face The dog-shaped front face panel with ears, together with two small round cardboard pieces. These give the Robot Dog its face and provide small mounting or spacer pieces for assembly. 7 Micro:bit with expansion board The electronic controller that runs the program and sends signals to connected components. 8 Servo motor and servo horns The small blue servo motor, its lead, and the white plastic horn attachments. The servo provides controlled movement to the mechanism.

Before you begin

Keep all the screws, nuts, servo horns, and small cardboard pieces in an order.

docs.title: Prepare for assembly
docs.text:
1. Check the cardboard pieces. Identify all pre-cut holes, slots, and fold lines. Do not punch extra holes unless the assembly instructions require them.
  2. Keep the electronics powered OFF. Do not connect or power the micro:bit while tightening the cardboard hardware.

docs.title: Final checklist
docs.text:
• All eight numbered part groups have been identified.
  • All fixed screws and nuts are secure.

docs.title: Robot Dog Head Assembly
docs.text: Let's assemble the Robot Dog's head! In this step, you will attach the two round cardboard pieces, secure the lower part of the face, and fold the forehead into position.

docs.title: Parts Required
docs.text: Part Quantity Purpose Robot Dog head cardboard 1 Main face, ears, and foldable forehead Round cardboard pieces 2 Reinforcement pieces on either side of the face White screws 3 Two to attach the round pieces and one for the bottom of the face Metal screw and nut 1 set Secures the folded forehead

docs.title: Step 1: Identify the head parts
docs.text: Place the head cardboard on a flat surface with the ears pointing upward. Find the three holes on the face and the hole on the forehead flap. Keep the two round cardboard pieces and all fasteners nearby.

docs.title: Step 2: Fix the round cardboard pieces
docs.text:
1. Place one round cardboard piece over the hole on the left side of the face.
  2. Align its center hole with the hole in the head cardboard.
  3. Insert one white screw to secure it.
  4. Repeat on the right side with the second round cardboard piece and another white screw.

Make sure both round pieces are aligned and sit flat against the cardboard.

docs.title: Step 3: Insert the bottom white screw
docs.text: Insert the third white screw through the hole at the bottom center of the face. Press it into place gently so it is secure.

docs.title: Step 4: Fold and secure the forehead
docs.text:
1. Locate the fold line on the forehead flap, between the two ears.
  2. Gently fold the forehead cardboard along the marked line.
  3. Align the forehead hole with the matching fixing point.
  4. Insert the metal screw and tighten it with the nut to hold the folded forehead in position.

Do not overtighten the metal screw, as it may damage the cardboard.

docs.title: Completed Head Assembly
docs.text: Your Robot Dog head is ready! Compare your assembled piece with the example above.

docs.title: Final Checklist
docs.text:
• Both round cardboard pieces are secured with one white screw each.
  • The third white screw is fixed at the bottom of the face.
  • The forehead flap is folded along its marked line.
  • The forehead is secured using one metal screw and one nut.
  • All fasteners are snug, and the cardboard is not bent or crushed.

Assembly tip

Fold the cardboard slowly along the marked line. If the holes do not line up, adjust the fold before tightening the screw rather than forcing the cardboard.

docs.title: Next Step
docs.text: Once the head is assembled, follow the next assembly step to attach it to the Robot Dog's neck and body.

docs.title: Final Assembly of the Brain on to the Robot Dog
docs.text:
In this step, we will coneect the Brain with the servo motor.

The expansion board helps us connect the Servo and power easily to the micro:bit.

docs.title: Parts Required
docs.text: Part Quantity Description Brain of the Robot Dog 1 Brain which controls the servo motor Servo motor 1 Servo motor connected for the movement

docs.title: 3. Connect the Servo Motor
docs.text:
Connect the Servo motor to P2 on the expansion board.

Servo wire connection:

Servo Wire Connect To Brown / Black GND Red VCC Orange / Yellow P2 Signal

Make sure the servo connector is inserted in the correct direction.

docs.title: 1. Place the Brain Controller on the Body
docs.text:
Place the micro:bit and expansion board assembly inside the Robot Dog body.

Position the board so that:

  • The micro:bit buttons and display face forward.
  • The board sits safely inside the body.
  • The servo wires can easily reach the expansion board.

docs.title: 2. Secure the Brain Using the Velcro Band
docs.text:
After placing the brain controller inside the Robot Dog body, use the Velcro band to hold it firmly in place.

Wrap the Velcro band around the Robot Dog body and the expansion board as shown in the image.

The Velcro band is important because it protects the brain controller from shaking or falling out while the Robot Dog is moving.

docs.title: Final Check
docs.text:
Before powering the Robot Dog, check the following:

  • Micro:bit is inserted in the correct direction.
  • All five screws on the micro:bit terminals are tightened properly.
  • Servo Motor wire is connected to P2.
  • VCC and GND connections are correct.
  • Servo wires are not blocking the movement.
  • Expansion board power switch is in the OFF position before connecting power.

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
• Do not reverse VCC and GND connections.
  • Do not overtighten the screws on the micro:bit.
  • Make sure the servo connectors are inserted in the correct direction.
  • If the servo motor does not move, check the P0 and P1 connections.
  • If the IR remote does not work, check the IR sensor connection on P2.

docs.title: Completed Step
docs.text:
The micro:bit and expansion board are now assembled.

The Robot Dog electronics are ready for programming and testing.

docs.title: Time to play
docs.text: Now it’s time to have fun with your Robot Dog, test its movements, and experiment with it.

docs.title: Attach the Robot Dog Head to the Neck
docs.text: Now that the Robot Dog head and neck mechanism are assembled, it is time to join them together. We will use the top screw already fixed to the forehead and the top hole in the neck cardboard piece.

docs.title: Parts Required
docs.text: Part Quantity Purpose Assembled Robot Dog head 1 The head prepared in the previous step Robot Dog body with neck attached 1 Supports the head and connects it to the servo mechanism Forehead screw 1 Already attached to the folded forehead of the head Nut 1 Secures the forehead screw to the neck

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
• Make sure the head is fully assembled, including the two round cardboard pieces and the lower white screw.
  • Check that the metal screw on the forehead is in place.
  • Locate the top hole on the long neck cardboard piece.
  • Turn OFF the expansion board before working on the assembly.

docs.title: Step 1: Identify the Forehead Screw
docs.text: Take the assembled head. Find the metal screw fitted through the folded cardboard tab in the middle of the forehead, between the two ears.

docs.title: Step 2: Align the Head with the Neck
docs.text:
Hold the head in front of the Robot Dog body, with its face looking forward.

  1. Bring the folded forehead tab towards the top of the neck.
  2. Line up the forehead screw with the top hole in the neck cardboard.
  3. Pass the existing screw through the neck hole carefully.

Do not make a new hole: use the top hole already provided in the neck piece.

docs.title: Step 3: Secure the Head
docs.text:
1. Place one nut onto the screw on the opposite side of the neck.
  2. Tighten the nut gently until the head is securely attached.
  3. Check that the head is centred and facing forward.

Caution

Do not overtighten the nut or crush the cardboard. Keep the connection secure without restricting the intended movement of the head mechanism.

docs.title: Step 4: Check the Finished Assembly
docs.text:
Your Robot Dog should now look like the assembled model below.

Check the following:

  • The forehead screw passes through the top neck hole.
  • The nut is fitted and the head does not wobble loosely.
  • The head faces forward and sits evenly on the body.
  • The head and neck have clearance to move without catching on the cardboard trunk.
  • Servo wires are free and are not trapped by the head or neck.

Do not force the servo shaft or head by hand. Once the wiring and program are ready, test the head movement through the servo controller.

docs.title: Assembly Video
docs.text: Your browser does not support the video tag.

docs.title: Next Step
docs.text: Great work! You have successfully attached the Robot Dog head to its neck. The head is now connected to the neck mechanism so it can move as the servo operates.

docs.title: Neck and Tail Assembly
docs.text:
In this step, we will attach the neck and tail to the Robot Dog trunk (body) prepared in the previous step. We will also connect both parts to the servo motor cardboard connector so that the servo motor can control the movement of the head and tail.

Follow the pictures and steps carefully. Do not switch ON the servo motor during assembly.

docs.title: Parts Required
docs.text:
Part Quantity Purpose Assembled trunk with servo motor horn 1 Body assembly completed in the previous step Neck cardboard piece (long one) 1 Connects to the head and provides head movement Tail cardboard piece (medium-length one) 1 Forms the moving tail Screws 4 One for the neck, one for the tail, and two for the body sides Nuts for the four screws 4 Hold the four screw connections in place Reused nuts 2 Secure the neck and tail connections to the servo cardboard connector

Total fasteners: 4 screws and 6 nuts (4 regular nuts + 2 reused nuts).

docs.title: Step 1: Identify the neck and tail
docs.text:
1. Take the long cardboard piece. This is the neck.
  2. Take the medium-length cardboard piece. This is the tail.
  3. Identify the marked fold lines and the pre-cut holes on both pieces.
  4. Gently fold along the marked lines as shown in the assembly reference. Do not bend or tear the cardboard at the holes.

docs.title: Step 2: Attach the neck to the body
docs.text:
1. Place the neck at the front of the trunk (longer side), where the Robot Dog's head will be attached.
  2. Align the neck hole with its matching mounting hole in the cardboard body.
  3. Insert 1 screw through the matching holes.
  4. Secure it with 1 nut. Tighten enough to hold the neck in place, but make sure its intended movement is not blocked.

docs.title: Step 3: Attach the tail to the body
docs.text:
1. Place the tail at the rear of the trunk (shorter side).
  2. Align its hole with the corresponding mounting hole on the body.
  3. Insert 1 screw through the matching holes.
  4. Secure it with 1 nut. Check that the tail is straight and has room to move.

docs.title: Step 4: Secure both sides of the body
docs.text:
1. Check that the folded sides of the trunk are aligned.
  2. Insert 1 screw and 1 nut on the left side of the body.
  3. Insert 1 screw and 1 nut on the right side of the body.
  4. Gently tighten both screws to keep the body shape firm.

At this point, you have used 4 screws and 4 nuts in total:

Connection Screws Nuts Neck to body 1 1 Tail to body 1 1 Left side of body 1 1 Right side of body 1 1 Total used 4 4

docs.title: Step 5: Connect the neck to the servo cardboard connector
docs.text:
1. Locate the servo motor cardboard connector installed during the servo horn assembly.
  2. Align the neck's connection point with the corresponding connector screw or threaded fixing point.
  3. Reuse the nut which is already in the servo motor cardboard connector and fit the neck onto the connector and secure the connection.
  4. Check that the neck remains connected while the servo linkage can move freely.

Important: Avoid overtightening a moving connection. The linkage should move without being pinched or bending the cardboard.

docs.title: Step 6: Connect the tail to the servo cardboard connector
docs.text:
1. Align the tail's connection point with the matching point on the servo motor cardboard connector.
  2. Reuse the nut which is already in the servo motor cardboard connector to secure the tail connection.
  3. Make sure the tail is properly aligned and does not rub against the trunk.

The 2 reused nuts now connect the neck and tail to the servo-operated cardboard linkage. This allows the servo motor to move the linked head/neck and tail mechanism.

docs.title: Step 7: Check the completed assembly
docs.text:
Compare your assembly with the reference picture below.

Check the following before proceeding:

  • Long neck piece is attached at the front.
  • Medium tail piece is attached at the back.
  • The body is secured with one screw and nut on each side.
  • One reused nut connects the neck to the servo cardboard connector.
  • One reused nut connects the tail to the servo cardboard connector.
  • All 4 screws and 6 nuts are accounted for.
  • Servo motor wire is free and not trapped between cardboard pieces.
  • The neck and tail can move without jamming.

Assembly tip: Keep the servo motor powered OFF while checking the linkage. Do not force the servo shaft by hand. If a connection feels tight, loosen its nut slightly and check the alignment before continuing.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: The micro:bit controls the servo motor. The servo moves the attached cardboard connector, which transfers motion to the neck and tail. Once the head is attached, the Robot Dog can move its head and tail as programmed.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem What to check Neck or tail does not move freely Check whether a nut is too tight or a cardboard part is misaligned Linkage comes loose Check the two reused nuts on the servo cardboard connector Body feels unstable Check the left and right body screws and nuts Cardboard bends or rubs Realign the neck, tail and connector before tightening Servo wire is pulled during movement Re-route the wire through the body with enough slack

docs.title: Completed Step
docs.text: Great job! The neck and tail assembly is now complete. Both parts are linked to the servo mechanism.

docs.text: After completing the setup, continue with the next step.

docs.title: Servo Motor Horn Setup
docs.text: In this step, we will assemble the servo motor connector and attach the servo horn to the servo motor. This mechanism connects the servo motor to the cardboard so that the robot can move it.

docs.title: Parts Required
docs.text:
Part Quantity Purpose Servo motor connector cardboard pieces 2 Rounded rectangular cardboard pieces that form the connector for the head or tail Screws and nuts 2 sets Secure the folded cardboard connector Servo motor 1 Produces movement for the head or tail mechanism White plastic servo horn 1 Transfers movement from the servo motor to the cardboard connector Small horn-mounting screws 3 Fasten the servo horn to the cardboard connector

Before starting: If you are using the servo-centering program, set the servo to its 90° initial position first and turn OFF the expansion board. Avoid rotating the servo shaft after centering it.

docs.title: Step 1: Fold the Servo Motor Connector Cardboard
docs.text:
1. Take the rounded-rectangle servo motor connector cardboard pieces shown above.
  2. Fold the connector along its marked fold line, following the shape demonstrated in the assembly video.
  3. Bring the ends together and align the screw holes.
  4. Insert 2 screws at the end of the folded cardboard and secure them with 2 nuts.
  5. Tighten gently until the connector holds its shape. Do not crush the cardboard.

docs.title: Step 2: Fix the Servo Horn to the Cardboard Connector
docs.text:
1. Take the white plastic servo horn supplied with the servo motor.
  2. Position the horn on the cardboard connector, aligning its mounting holes with the prepared holes in the cardboard.
  3. Insert 2 small screws near the ends of the servo horn to fasten the horn to the connector.
  4. Check that the horn is firmly attached and sits straight.

docs.title: Step 3: Attach the Connector to the Servo Motor
docs.text:
1. Take the servo motor and orient its shaft toward the attached horn.
  2. Carefully push the servo motor into the folded cardboard connector, as demonstrated in the video.
  3. Align the center of the horn and connector with the servo motor shaft. Press the horn onto the shaft without forcing it.
  4. Take the remaining small servo screw and insert it through the middle of the cardboard/horn assembly into the center of the servo motor shaft.
  5. Tighten the center screw gently so the cardboard connector and horn remain fixed to the servo motor.

Do not force the servo motor

Do not twist the servo shaft by hand or overtighten the screws. Keep the servo cable clear of the moving connector.

docs.title: Step 4: Check the Assembly
docs.text:
• The cardboard connector is folded neatly.
  • Both connector screws and nuts are secure.
  • The horn is fixed to the cardboard with its 2 small screws.
  • The center screw holds the horn onto the servo motor shaft.
  • The cardboard connector is straight and does not rub against the servo housing.
  • The servo wire is free and not pinched.

docs.title: Assembly Video
docs.text:
Follow the video to see how the cardboard connector, servo horn, and servo motor are fitted together.

Your browser does not support the video tag.

docs.title: Completed Step
docs.text:
The servo motor horn and cardboard connector assembly is ready to be attached to the Robot Dog head or tail, as shown in the next assembly steps.

After completing the servo horn setup, continue with the next step.

docs.title: Robot Dog Trunk Assembly
docs.text: In this step, we will make the trunk (body) of the Robot Dog from the pre-cut cardboard and insert the servo motor horn assembly prepared in the previous step. The trunk supports the head and tail mechanism, so fold it carefully and keep the servo wires free.

docs.title: Parts Required
docs.text: Part Quantity Purpose Trunk cardboard piece 1 Pre-cut main body with marked fold lines and a rectangular servo opening Servo motor horn assembly 1 Servo motor with its previously assembled cardboard connector and horn

docs.title: 1. Identify the Trunk Cardboard
docs.text:
Take the trunk cardboard piece shown below. Find the marked fold lines, the rectangular opening in the centre, and the small fixing holes.

Before folding, check that the cardboard is not damaged and that the rectangular opening is clear.

docs.title: 2. Fold the Trunk on All Sides
docs.text:
1. Place the trunk cardboard on a flat surface.
  2. Gently fold along each marked line, working around all the sides of the cardboard.
  3. Raise the side panels and fold the end flaps inward to form the trunk shape, as demonstrated in the assembly video.
  4. Keep the folds straight so that the panels fit together neatly.
  5. Make sure the rectangular opening remains accessible for the servo motor.

Tip

Fold a little at a time along the scored lines. Avoid bending the cardboard at an unmarked position, as it may tear.

docs.title: 3. Take the Prepared Servo Motor Horn
docs.text:
Use the servo motor horn assembly completed in the previous step. The picture below shows the servo attached to its cardboard connector.

Before fitting the assembly:

  • Confirm that the servo horn and cardboard connector are securely attached.
  • Keep the servo motor powered OFF.
  • If the servo has already been set to its starting position, do not rotate its shaft or horn by hand.

docs.title: 4. Insert the Servo Motor Horn Assembly at the Top
docs.text:
1. Locate the rectangular opening in the trunk cardboard.
  2. Position the prepared servo motor assembly at the top of the trunk, as shown in the reference image.
  3. Carefully guide the servo motor into the opening and seat the horn connector in its intended position.
  4. Adjust the folded cardboard panels around the assembly so that it fits neatly, without forcing the servo or crushing the cardboard.
  5. Route the servo wire through the open space so that it is not pinched between the folded panels.

The following image shows the trunk with the servo motor inserted and the wire routed outside the opening.

Warning

Do not pull on the servo cable or force the servo into the cutout. Check its orientation against the assembly image before pressing it into place.

docs.title: 5. Check the Assembly
docs.text:
Before moving on, verify that:

  • All sides of the trunk are folded along their marked lines.
  • The trunk holds its intended shape.
  • The servo motor horn assembly is positioned at the top.
  • The servo motor fits into the rectangular opening.
  • The servo wire is free and is not trapped under the cardboard.
  • The horn and connector remain firmly attached.

docs.title: Completed Step
docs.text: The Robot Dog trunk is now folded, and the servo motor horn assembly is in position.

docs.text: After completing the setup, continue with the next step.

docs.title: Expansion Board and Micro:bit Assembly
docs.text:
In this step, we will assemble the micro:bit onto the expansion board and calibrate the servo motors

The expansion board helps us connect the servoe motor and power easily from the micro:bit.

docs.title: Parts Required
docs.text: Part Quantity Description Micro:bit 1 Main controller board Expansion board 1 Used to connect servo motors, IR sensor, and power Small screws 5 Used to tighten the micro:bit onto the expansion board Servo motor 1 Servo motor used for the movement mechanism

docs.title: 1. Place the Micro:bit on the Expansion Board
docs.text:
Take the micro:bit and place it on the expansion board as shown.

Make sure the gold edge connector pins of the micro:bit align properly with the expansion board terminals.

The micro:bit pins should match the labels on the expansion board:

Micro:bit Pin Expansion Board Terminal 0 P0 / 0 1 P1 / 1 2 P2 / 2 3V V / 3V GND G / GND

docs.title: 2. Tighten the Micro:bit Screws
docs.text:
After placing the micro:bit correctly on the expansion board, use the screws to secure it.

Tighten the screws on the following terminals:

  • P0 / 0
  • P1 / 1
  • P2 / 2
  • 3V / V
  • GND / G

Do not overtighten the screws. Tighten them just enough so that the micro:bit makes proper contact with the expansion board.

docs.title: 3. Connect the Servo Motor
docs.text:
Connect the servo motor to P2 on the expansion board and calibrate which is essential for assembly

Servo wire connection:

Servo Wire Connect To Brown / Black GND Red VCC Orange / Yellow P2 Signal

Make sure the servo connector is inserted in the correct direction.

Check the following:

  • Micro:bit is inserted in the correct direction.
  • All five screws on the micro:bit terminals are tightened properly.
  • Servo Motor is connected to P2.
  • VCC and GND connections are correct.
  • Expansion board power switch is in the OFF position before connecting power.

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
• Do not reverse VCC and GND connections.
  • Do not overtighten the screws on the micro:bit.
  • Make sure the servo connectors are inserted in the correct direction.

docs.title: If You Want to Program It Yourself Using MakeCode
docs.text: Use this method if the robot program is not already pre programmed in the micro:bit.

docs.title: 1. Connect the Micro:bit
docs.text: Connect the micro:bit to your computer using a USB cable.

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
• Open the above program in https://makecode.microbit.org/ by clicking on Edit Code and clicking on the arrow.

  • Click download and program the code.

docs.title: Servo Motor Initial Position Setup
docs.text:
Before assembling the Robot Dog , the servo motors must be set to their initial position. This step is important because the servo horn position decides how it will move.

Follow these steps:

  1. Insert the micro:bit into the expansion board.
  2. Connect the first servo motor to the expansion board.
  3. Turn ON the power switch on the expansion board.
  4. The servo motor will automatically move to the initial center position.
  5. Turn OFF the power switch on the expansion board.
  6. Do not rotate or disturb the servo shaft after it reaches initial position.

Warning

Do not disturb the servo horn or servo shaft after setting the servo to initial position. If the position changes, the Robot Dog movement may not work properly.

docs.title: Play and Experiment with Robot Dog
docs.text:
Now it is time to have fun with your Robot Dog, test its movements, and explore new experiments with your own robot pet dog.

You can control the Robot Dog:

Using the Bluetooth Web Control App

https://remote.stemsmartlabs.com/

docs.title: 2. Pair the Micro:bit
docs.text:
Follow these steps to connect your Robot Dog:

  1. Power ON the Robot Dog using the switch on the expansion board.
  2. Open the Bluetooth Web Control App:

https://remote.stemsmartlabs.com/

  1. Click PAIR MICROBIT.

docs.title: 3. Use D-Pad Controls
docs.text:
After the micro:bit is connected, use the D-Pad controls on the web app to move the Robot Dog.

D-Pad Button Robot Dog Action Up Move forward Down Move backward Left Turn left Right Turn right Center / Stop Stop movement Wiggle Wiggle the head and tail

The Robot Dog will respond to the direction selected from the web control app.

docs.title: 4. Safety and Usage Tips
docs.text:
• Use the Robot Dog on a flat surface.
  • Do not pull the servo wires while it is moving.
  • Keep fingers away from the moving legs.
  • Make sure the micro:bit and expansion board are secured using the Velcro band.
  • Turn OFF the power switch after use.
  • If it get stuck, turn OFF the power before adjusting them.

docs.title: 5. Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Possible Reason Solution Web app does not find micro:bit Bluetooth is off or micro:bit is not powered Turn ON Bluetooth and power ON the Robot Dog Micro:bit pairs but does not respond Program may not be loaded correctly Recheck and upload the Robot Dog program Servo does not move Servo wire is loose Check P2 servo connections Robot Dog stops suddenly Power may be low Replace or recharge the battery

docs.title: Completed
docs.text:
Congratulations! You have successfully built and tested your own DIY Robot Dog Top Kit.

Enjoy playing and experimenting with your own robot pet dog.

docs.title: Robot Unicorn Experiment
docs.text:
Experiment building the Robot Unicorn head and replace the Robot Dog head.

Let's give your robot a magical unicorn head! In this step, you will fold the cardboard head, secure its shape, attach the two round side pieces, and connect the finished head to the robot's neck.

docs.title: Parts Required
docs.text:
Part Quantity Purpose Unicorn head cardboard 1 Forms the face, ears, and unicorn horn Round cardboard pieces 2 Attach to both sides of the face Metal screws 3 Two to hold the bottom of the folded head and one to attach the head to the neck Metal nuts 3 Secure the three metal screws White plastic screws 2 Fix the two round cardboard pieces Assembled robot body with neck 1 Supports the completed unicorn head

Before you start

Identify the fold lines and all the holes in the head cardboard. Keep the robot switched OFF while assembling.

docs.title: Step 1: Fold the Unicorn Head
docs.text:
1. Place the unicorn head cardboard on a flat surface.
  2. Gently fold it along the pre-marked lines to form the head.
  3. Bring the side sections into position so the head takes shape.
  4. Keep the ears and pointed unicorn horn upright.

Avoid forcing the cardboard. Fold slowly to prevent tearing along the crease lines.

docs.title: Step 2: Secure the Bottom of the Head
docs.text:
1. Align the holes in the folded cardboard at the bottom of the head.
  2. Insert two metal screws, one through each matching bottom fixing point.
  3. Attach one nut to each screw.
  4. Tighten gently until the folded head holds its shape.

Used in this step: 2 metal screws + 2 nuts.

docs.title: Step 3: Attach the Two Round Cardboard Pieces
docs.text:
1. Take the two round cardboard pieces.
  2. Place one on each side of the unicorn's face, aligned with the side holes.
  3. Insert a white plastic screw through each round piece and its matching hole.
  4. Press the plastic screws into place so both round pieces sit securely.

Used in this step: 2 round pieces + 2 white plastic screws.

Note

Both round pieces should be fitted evenly on opposite sides of the face, as shown in the reference image.

docs.title: Step 4: Fold the Top Tab Between the Ears
docs.text:
1. Locate the small cardboard tab between the unicorn's ears, beneath the pointed horn.
  2. Fold the tab along its marked line.
  3. Insert the remaining metal screw through the hole in this folded top tab.
  4. Leave the screw ready to connect to the robot's neck.

Used in this step: 1 metal screw. Keep the last nut for the next step.

docs.title: Step 5: Connect the Unicorn Head to the Neck
docs.text:
1. Hold the completed unicorn head in front of the robot's neck.
  2. Align the screw in the top folded tab with the top hole of the neck.
  3. Pass the screw through the neck hole.
  4. Fasten it using the remaining nut.
  5. Check that the unicorn head faces forward and is attached securely.

Used in this step: 1 nut.

docs.title: Completed Unicorn Head
docs.text: Your robot now has a unicorn head with two ears and a pointed horn!

docs.title: Final Assembly Checklist
docs.text:
• Cardboard is folded neatly along the marked lines.
  • Two screws and nuts hold the bottom of the head together.
  • The two round side pieces are fixed with white plastic screws.
  • The tab between the ears is folded correctly.
  • The top screw passes through the neck hole and is secured with the final nut.
  • The head is aligned and securely attached.
  • The head and neck can move without the cardboard snagging or servo wires getting pulled.

Handle with care

Do not overtighten the metal screws or force the cardboard folds. After connecting the head, check its movement gently before turning the robot on. Keep fingers clear of moving parts.

docs.title: What's Next?
docs.text: Once the head is securely attached, continue with the remaining robot assembly and testing steps. You can also draw eyes, a smile, and colourful details to give your Robot Unicorn its own personality!

docs.title: Neo Beginner Kit for BBC Microbit
docs.text:
The Neo Beginner Kit for BBC Microbit is designed for beginners to easily explore electronics, coding, and real-world problem solving.

With the BBC micro:bit at its core and a kit full of sensors, actuators, display, and modules, this kit empowers learners to build hands-on projects—from smart devices to automation systems without any breadboarding or soldering. All modules are connected using the pre-terminated cables included in the kit, making the entire experience plug-and-play and beginner-friendly.

docs.title: Temperature & Humidity

docs.title: Smart Plant Watering System
docs.text: The Smart Plant Watering System is a beginner-friendly automation project that uses the micro:bit and the sensors in your Neo Beginner Kit to automatically water a plant based on soil moisture levels. This project introduces students to environment sensing, conditional automation, and safe control of external devices using a relay and water pump.

docs.title: What It Does
docs.text:
The system continuously monitors the soil moisture sensor.

  • If the soil is dry, the micro:bit activates the relay, turning ON the water pump to water the plant.

  • If the soil is wet enough, the pump remains OFF. The OLED display shows real-time soil readings and watering status, making it easier to understand how the system behaves.

This forms the foundation for environmental automation systems used in agriculture and home gardening.

docs.title: Hardware Used
docs.text:
This project uses the following modules from the Neo Beginner Kit:

  • Soil Moisture Sensor – Detects dryness or moisture in the soil

  • NeoPixel Ring – Shows whether the plant is happy (green) or sad (red)

  • Relay Module – Safely turns the pump ON and OFF

  • Water Pump + Tube – Pumps water into the plant

  • OLED Display (I2C) – Shows moisture level and pump status

  • Breakout Board + Connection Cables – Plug-and-play connections to micro:bit

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
• The soil moisture sensor sends an analog value to the micro:bit.

  • The micro:bit compares this value to a threshold (dry vs. wet).

  • If the soil is dry, the micro:bit triggers the relay, powering the water pump.

  • The pump runs for a few seconds and then stops to avoid overwatering.

✅ Once you understand how smart plant watering system works, you can expand this idea into different areas of agriculture.

docs.text: The Neo Inventor Kit for BBC Microbit works seamlessly with the official Microsoft MakeCode Editor. MakeCode provides a friendly, browser-based environment where you can program the micro:bit using Blocks, JavaScript, or Python—making it suitable for both beginners and advanced learners.

docs.title: Install the Neo Inventor kit for Microbit Makecode extension
docs.text:
1. Open https://makecode.microbit.org in your browser.

2. Click on New Project and create a project.

3. In the MakeCode editor, click on the Extensions menu.

4. In the search box, paste the GitHub URL:

https://github.com/STEMSmartLabs/neo-inventor-kit-microbit and press Enter, then click on the extension to install it.

Once installed, you will see the Neo Inventor Kit category in the MakeCode blocks panel.

docs.title: Points to remember when using Neo Inventor Kit
docs.text:
1. Always initialize the kit by using initialize Neo Inventor kit in the on start block in all your projects.
  2. It will disable microbit onboard LED since these pins are used by the Neo Inventor kit so duing the boot this initialization happens because of which you will see the fan and buzzer turning on and off.
  3. Do not use the microbit onboard 25 LEDs in the projects which means do not use show blocks under the Basic category use only the OLED display blocks under Neo Inventor Kit category since it is now remapped.
